      <cbc:Description languageID="ENG">ECMWF, as the Entrusted Entity for the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS), invites Tenders for Co-design of GHG policy services in support of EU Member States and Copernicus Participating countries
ECMWF intends to award a single Framework Agreement for a period of maximum 22 months, which shall be implemented via a single multi-annual Service Contract expected to commence in Q1 2027.</cbc:Description>
      <cbc:ProcurementTypeCode listName="contract-nature">services</cbc:ProcurementTypeCode>
      <cbc:Note languageID="ENG">Procedure to be applied: The procurement will be conducted in accordance with ECMWF's procedures as set out in Invitation to Tender documents, which are available on ECMWF's eProcurement Portal (https://procurement.ecmwf.int/) and no other procedures will apply. In submitting this notice ECMWF does not waive the privileges and immunities granted to it by virtue of its status as an intergovernmental organisation or submit itself to any jurisdiction. Tenders must be submitted using ECMWF's eProcurement Portal. Hard copy (paper) submissions will not be accepted.
Due to the need to include performance and compliance obligations in the contract, ECMWF will contract only with a single legal person or entity which is competent to undertake and commit to these obligations. ECMWF recognises that some bids will involve a number of organisations which may wish to work together to deliver the contract requirements. In such cases, these organisations must identify a lead contractor who will sign the contract with ECMWF and who will be responsible for putting in place legal arrangements to ensure that it can guarantee that all other organisations will also meet the contract obligations. ECMWF will not enter into multiple contracts with individual members of consortia or groups of service providers.
Eligibility: Refer to Section 3.2 of Volume I of the ITT documents.</cbc:Note>

         <cbc:Description languageID="ENG">The successful bidder will propose the interaction with national inventory agencies and related institutes that are responsible for national monitoring of GHG emissions and the reporting to the UNFCCC . 
The successful Tenderer shall carry out the following activities:
•	Detailed familiarisation of the successful Tenderer with the latest status of current and emerging operational CAMS products and the use of satellite Earth Observations (EO) for GHG emissions monitoring. 
•	Facilitate collaboration between European national inventory agencies and CAMS.

•	Provide recommendations for the development of policy-relevant tools, including data visualisation,  at national level.</cbc:Description>

normalized.description: ESA intends to implement a Zero Debris policy by 2030 and has a long-term vision for a sustainable and safe space environment leveraging on the development of a space circular economy.Large Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites in particular present significant risks, both in terms of potential collisions and ground casualty hazards resulting from uncontrolled re-entry. normalized.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop a European beamforming chip IP core based on ultra-deep sub-micron technology for satcom constellations. Power consumption shall be minimised. Selectable waveform specific features shall be implemented to support a wide range of use cases including pre-coding and beam hopping. A test chip with compatible interfaces to high speed SerDes (Serialiser/Deserialiser) providing reliable connectivity for high throughput satellites of LEO and MEO constellations shall be designed and manufactured.Targeted Improvements: - Enabling a European or Canadian source of digital beamforming IP core for active phased array antennas.- Enabling features such as signal structure, beam hopping and precoding.- Minimised power consumption of less than 300mW per channel.Description: Due to the demand for large capacity and high spectral efficiencies, active array antennas are being increasingly employed for telecom satellites. These antennas are already playing an important role in next-generation high throughput satellite (HTS) communications together with the large low Earth orbit (LEO) and medium Earth orbit (MEO) constellations being implemented worldwide. Digital Beamforming (DBF) is considered the most flexible beamforming architecture and has advantages over analogue beamforming for receiving and transmitting wideband signals, and for multi-beam reconfigurable applications. However, it requires data converters and RF front-ends for each antenna element, increasing the complexity and power consumption.In this activity, a digital beamforming IP core will be developed, fabricated as a scaled Engineering Model test chip and tested based on ultra sub-micron technology (targeting 7nm or lower). Power consumption shall be minimised, targeting 300mW per channel. Selectable waveform specific features shall be implemented to support a wide range of use casesincluding pre-coding and beam hopping. The IP core shall enable Beamforming Networks with a total bandwidth scalable from GHz to hundreds of GHz for dynamic beam configuration, to achieve a BFIC of 32 GHz capacity with scalable frequency from L-Band to Ka-Band and frequency agnostic topology.This activity will be implemented in a phased approach where:- Phase 1 includes a comparative architectural study of at least four digital beam forming IC integration models. An evaluation of technology node implications shall be performed (e.g. leading-edge vs. trailing-edge). Phase 1 shall explore if a common architecture could support different use-cases (broadband, D2D) e.g. lowering DAC/ADC sampling rates and smart switching (bypassing digital mixing, decimation/interpolation) to maintain beam count while adjusting per-beam bandwidth. A system topology shall be evaluated and defined from the digital processor to the antenna for the placement of the beamforming network (daisy chain, star etc.). The output of Phase 1 is an evaluation of the critical IP blocks via design simulation concluding with tape-out of the design. Phase 1 budget is up to 1,200kEur.- In Phase 2 the architecture and technology for the beamforming chip IP shall be fully designed, implemented and tested to scaled engineering model level. This test chip will be representative of a scaled version of the final potential product. Scaled EM testing will include radiation exposure, thermal cycling, and performance benchmarking against existing space-grade beamforming chips.IP cores developed in this activity shall be available for further development by ESA Member State and Canadian industries at fair and reasonable market conditions.

The S2NG space segment is expected to comprise of a constellation of two identical satellites (A- and B-units) flying at an altitude of approximately 650 km, in a sun-synchronous orbit. ESA/ESEC is the ESA European Space Security and Education Centre located in Belgium and is one of the ESA sites in Europe. The main core business in Mission Operations relevant to this procurement are:  Control dedicated Satellites and Ground Segment (so called "Small Satellite missions")  Perform its In-Orbit activities.  Host and operate some ground segment elements in support to the EU Space Programme within a secured environment - mainly Galileo and EGNOS The Operational services, within the scope specified above, will be therefore divided in two main WPs: WP-1 Small Satellites Operations:   A number of Small Satellites (such as the PROBA ones) are or will be controlled from ESEC with the help of a dedicated ground segment. In the current set-up and number of missions, up to six passes per satellite daily are supported in automatic mode for TM reception and commanding, which may be extended in the future when new missions will be operated from ESEC. The mission products are made available at ESEC and ready for distribution. The Small Satellites Mission Operations Centre is therefore responsible of the monitoring and control of the satellite and the corresponding ground segment, the handling of the user requests, the extraction of the mission products and their availability for distribution.  The Small Satellites operations concept relies on a highly automatic functioning of the ground segment and a high degree of autonomy in the space segment for the delayed execution of operations requested by telecommand and for satellite survival. No operator attended shift work is foreseen. Operational engineers supervise the small satellites mission operations and related performances usually only during normal working hours. Provisions for an On-Call service shall be also considered for the WP. Occasional working outside normal working hours and overtime may be required. The satellites are safe by design and can survive for a long period without ground station contact.   This WP will cover OPSPREP and OPS activities, support to Industry, execution of delegated tasks for critical operations (LEOP, others) together and in collaboration with Industry for this small satellite missions. This WP may implement further mission operations engineering activities carried out in support of other ESA programmes requested by ESA programme directorates to OPS. WP-2 Galileo Hosting activities:  The Galileo Hosting support will be provided in response to the requirements and agreements reached with EUSPA for Galileo and EGNOS. The provision of support to the hosting and testing activities will be performed on-site during normal working hours. Provisions for an On-Call service shall be also considered for the WP. Occasional working outside normal working hours and overtime may be required. The Agency will issue one single Invitation to Tender in Open Competition for the two WPs. Considering the relatively small volume covered by this procurement, the Tenderers will be invited to provide a single proposal covering the support to both areas.   The new contract is planned to be kicked-off starting in 1st Quarter 2027 (phase-in) as required to permit sufficient time for a smooth transition (e.g. training, certification of new service provider's personnel).  The operational phase of the contract is expected to start latest by 2nd Quarter 2027, at the expiry of the current INDUSTRIAL SERVICE PROVISION IN SUPPORT OF THE OPERATION OF ESA IN BELGIUM contract extension.
